definitions.explanation: A person who flies aircraft. More formal than パイロット.
Used in the compound {宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし} to mean astronaut.

examples.japanese: {飛行士|ひこうし}になるのが{夢|ゆめ}だ。
examples.english: My dream is to become a pilot.

examples.japanese: {宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし}が{無事|ぶじ}に{地球|ちきゅう}に{帰還|きかん}した。
examples.english: The astronaut safely returned to Earth.

examples.japanese: {日本人|にほんじん}の{宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし}が{国際|こくさい}{宇宙|うちゅう}ステーションで{活動|かつどう}している。
examples.english: A Japanese astronaut is working on the International Space Station.

examples.japanese: テスト{飛行士|ひこうし}が{新型|しんがた}の{航空機|こうくうき}を{操縦|そうじゅう}した。
examples.english: A test pilot flew the new aircraft.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}から{飛行士|ひこうし}に{憧|あこが}れ、{厳|きび}しい{訓練|くんれん}を{経|へ}てようやくその{夢|ゆめ}を{叶|かな}えた。
examples.english: He had admired pilots since childhood and finally fulfilled that dream after rigorous training.

examples.japanese: {娘|むすめ}は{宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし}になりたいと{言|い}って、{毎日|まいにち}{星|ほし}の{図鑑|ずかん}を{読|よ}んでいる。
examples.english: My daughter says she wants to be an astronaut and reads a book about stars every day.

notes:
{飛行士|ひこうし} is the formal term for a person who operates aircraft, formed from {飛行|ひこう} (flight) + {士|し} (professional/practitioner). The {士|し} suffix denotes a qualified professional, giving the word a more formal tone than the loanword パイロット.

KEY COMPOUND:
- {宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし} — astronaut (literally "space pilot")

RELATED WORDS:
- パイロット — pilot (loanword, more common in everyday use)
- {操縦士|そうじゅうし} — pilot (emphasizes the operation of the aircraft)
